title: Micro LLM Usage Playbook — sketch
summary: Personal scratchpad for a lightweight operational playbook to route to smaller/cheaper models when appropriate — ideas, user stories, quick acceptance criteria and open questions.
content:
Context / why:
- We have a growing catalog of small/medium open models (7B-13B) and micro models (<=3B) that are much cheaper per token. For many short-turn tasks (autocomplete, system prompts, simple Q&A) we can get 80–95% of required quality at a fraction of the cost.
- Need a pragmatic, ops-friendly playbook for teams to safely use micro models without surprising regressions for end-users. This is a personal sketch — not a formal PRD yet.

Problem statement (short):
- Product teams want predictable unit economics. Many requests don't need top-tier models but there is no standardized way to (a) pick cheaper models, (b) measure regressions, and (c) roll back safely.

Goals:
- Reduce per-request cost for suitable workloads by 30–60% via automatic or opt-in micro-model routing.
- Keep visible safety net: easy fallback to higher-fidelity models when quality drops.
- Low operational burden: guided defaults, telemetry for regressions, and a simple rollout path.

Non-goals:
- This is NOT about replacing large models for heavy reasoning tasks.
- Not building full eval lab here — rely on existing eval infra for periodic checks.

Proposed primitives / features (brainstorm):
1) Micro-profile descriptors
   - Light metadata for each micro model: tokens-per-dollar, latency_p50_p95, sweet_spots (seq_len), strengths/weaknesses (summarization/short Q&A), sample prompts where it fails.
   - Stored as small JSON 'model-card-mini' for quick routing heuristics.

2) Request classifier (cheap heuristic)
   - Fast client-side or gateway classifier that tags requests as 'micro-safe' / 'maybe' / 'no'. Use sequence length, instruction type, expected output length, presence of tools, and simple intent keywords.
   - Keep it probabilistic: ~90% recall for 'micro-safe' to avoid false negatives.

3) Tiered routing policy (configurable per-route)
   - Default: try micro-model, if quality-check (see below) passes then serve; else fallback to standard model.
   - Modes: always-micro, auto-tier (try then fallback), manual (developer picks model).

4) Lightweight quality gate / pulse-check
   - For a sampled fraction of micro responses, run a parallel judge: compare micro output vs baseline on cheap eval (embedding similarity, n-gram overlap, heuristic classifiers).
   - If drift exceeds threshold (e.g., embedding similarity < 0.8 for >X% traffic), automatically trigger canary rollback or alert.

5) Canary rollouts + traffic shaping
   - Start at 1% of route traffic -> 5% -> 20% with automated checks at each step (latency, token-cost, quality gate).
   - Fast cutover / rollback button in Console.

6) Model fallback pre-emptive cache
   - If micro model returns low-confidence token(s), fetch continuation from higher-fidelity model for that response or re-run full request. Avoid user-facing latency by async patching for non-interactive flows.

7) Developer UX: hints + simulation mode
   - 'Simulate' mode: run traffic through micro routing but report hypothetical cost savings + quality deltas without serving to users.
   - In the Console: suggested model profiles for each route based on historical metrics.

8) Billing/metrics: show per-route token $ delta, p50/p95 latency, and regression alarms in same view.

User stories (raw):
- As a product engineer, I want to enable 'micro-mode' for the autocomplete route so that 80% of quick completions are served from a <3B model and I can see cost and quality impact in 24h.
- As an SRE, I want automatic rollback if the sampled micro responses drop below similarity threshold so customer experience isn't degraded.
- As a platform owner, I want a one-click simulation that shows predicted annual cost savings if 50% of route X is served by micro models.

Acceptance criteria (initial):
- Routing config can be enabled per-route and rolls out to traffic percentages.
- Telemetry shows per-model token usage and cost delta within 15 mins of traffic.
- Quality gating detects significant drop (configurable) and triggers rollback/alert.

Metrics to monitor:
- Cost-per-1000-requests delta (baseline vs micro).
- Quality-similarity score (embedding cosine) sample rate 1% or 0.1% depending on volume.
- False rollback rate (cases where rollback happened but users didn't notice).
- Latency p50/p95 impact.

Risks and mitigations: 
- Hidden semantic regressions (mitigate via human-in-the-loop sampling for critical flows).
- Increased operational complexity for teams — provide sane defaults and a 'one-click simulate' to lower barrier.
- Attack surface: micro models might behave differently for adversarial inputs—add adversarial tests to evals.

Quick tech notes / rough architecture sketch: 
- Gateway inspects request -> classifier -> route decision -> (optionally) fork sample to judge -> serve.
- Judge can be embedding-based (micro output vs baseline), or cheap heuristic. Keep judge work off the main request path for latency-critical flows (do async checks + corrective actions).

Rollout plan (very rough):
1) Internal alpha: product infra + single route (autocomplete) in simulate mode. 2) Closed beta: enable auto-tier with 1% traffic, sample judge 5% of micro responses. 3) Public opt-in: expose simple toggle and Console simulation. 4) Gradual default: suggest micro-mode to high-volume routes after 2 weeks of stable metrics.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- What is an acceptable similarity threshold by route type? (short Q&A vs code completion vs instruction) -> spike: run historical evals. (Ticket INF-2413?)
- Sampling rate tradeoffs: cost of judge vs detection sensitivity. Need an experiment.
- How to show 'why micro failed' in Console (example deltas, sample pairs).
- Decide default classifier heuristics; maybe use tiny transformer classifier hosted as a microservice? pros/cons.
- API ergonomics: should developer pass a hint ("micro_hint": "low_fidelity") or rely entirely on route config? Mixed mode?

Notes-to-self / friction points:
- Keep model-card-mini small and machine-readable. Don't re-invent complex model cards.
- Console UX: show sample micro vs baseline diffs with red/green badges, but simple — teams won't read long tables.

References / links:
- INF-2413: micro-model profiler (ticket).
- RED-309: mini-model profiles in Linear.
- Slack: #model-routing thread (search for "micro-mode")

Small mock flows (CLI):
- enable: redwood routes update autocomplete --micro-mode auto-tier --sample-judge-rate 0.02
- simulate: redwood routes simulate autocomplete --micro-mode auto-tier --history 7d

Final quick takeaways (for next sync):
- Build minimal model-card-mini + a classifier + simulate mode first. Low friction path to show wins.
- Push hard on Console visibility for costs and a clear rollback.
- Pair early with a single product team (autocomplete / snippets) for measurable delta.
